title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and seafood is a home recipe (3659). Whole grain pasta retains bran and germ, increasing fiber and micronutrient content. The tomato sauce, made from ripe tomatoes, provides lycopene and vitamin C, while seafood (shrimp, mussels, squid) adds protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta has a lower glycemic index than refined white pasta.
Tomatoes used in the sauce are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart health.
Seafood is one of the best natural sources of iodine, essential for thyroid function.
Making the sauce at home lets you control salt and sugar levels, making the dish healthier.
In Italy, whole‑grain pasta is traditionally called "pasta integrale".

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and stable blood glucose.

items.title: Plant protein source
items.content: Whole grain flour supplies about 12 g of protein per 100 g, beneficial for vegetarians.

items.title: Lycopene and vitamin C
items.content: Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene and vitamin C, which boost immunity and have anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood delivers EPA and DHA omega‑3s, important for heart and brain health.

items.title: Minerals (iodine, zinc, iron)
items.content: Shrimp and mussels provide iodine, zinc, and iron, essential for metabolism and immune function.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or squid, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; monitor sodium intake, especially for people with hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne toxins
items.content: Improperly stored seafood can develop histamine or other toxins that cause food poisoning.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten and is unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, topped with the tomato‑seafood sauce. Garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, or a drizzle of olive oil. For a lighter texture, cook the pasta al dente.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep dry pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked sauce and seafood should be refrigerated and consumed within 2‑3 days, or frozen in a sealed container for up to one month.
